values.title: Seasonal Italian cooking on North Clark Street
values.text: Handmade pasta, a wood-fired hearth and a menu that follows Midwest farms through the year. Dinner Tuesday to Sunday, and long lunches on Sundays.

image.alt: The candlelit dining room at Hazel on a busy evening, with the brick oven glowing behind the marble bar

values.title: Pasta rolled every afternoon, vegetables we know by name
values.body:
Chef Marta Kowalczyk cooks the food she learned in Bologna with whatever Illinois and Wisconsin farms bring to our back door that week. The menu changes six times a year.

  • Bread, pasta and gelato made here every day
  • Meat and fish cooked over oak in the old bakery oven
  • 120 wines, mostly from small Italian growers

values.title: What people say on the way home

items.quote: The pumpkin cappellacci are reason enough to cross the city on a Tuesday. Order a second plate, because nobody at the table will want to share.
items.name: Nadia Brooks

items.quote: We came for our anniversary in 2021 and now we have a standing Thursday table. Daniel remembers what we drank last time, which is more than we do.
items.name: Ellen Park

items.quote: Hazel cooks as if the Midwest had always been part of Italy: whitefish in brown butter, quince in the olive oil cake and a short rib you can cut with a spoon.
items.name: Marcus Hale

items.quote: The bar is my favorite seat in the neighborhood. A glass of Lambrusco, a plate of cacio e pepe and the kitchen right in front of you.

values.title: A neighborhood osteria in an old Swedish bakery
values.text: Hazel opened on Clark Street in April 2019, in the room where Lindqvist’s Bakery sold cardamom buns for 65 years. We kept the brick oven, added a long marble bar and filled the place with pasta.

image.alt: The front of Hazel at dusk, with the old Lindqvist’s Bakery lettering still painted above the window

values.title: Named after the best cook either of us knew
values.left:
Marta Kowalczyk grew up above her parents’ deli in Avondale and spent three years in a trattoria in Bologna, where she learned to roll pasta by hand before the lunch rush.

Back in Chicago she ran North Side kitchens for a decade and kept a notebook of the farmers whose vegetables she wanted to cook for herself.
values.right:
Daniel Okafor met Marta on the same Logan Square line in 2012. He moved to the dining room, then to wine, and never stopped talking about his grandmother Hazel, who fed half of her block in Bronzeville every Sunday.

When Lindqvist’s closed in 2016, they signed the lease, kept the oven and named the restaurant after her.

values.quote: We cook what the farms send us that week. If the squash is better than the recipe, the squash wins.
values.name: Marta Kowalczyk

values.title: Thirty-one farms, most within 200 miles
values.intro: We buy whole animals, whole crates and whatever the weather allows. These six decide what is on the menu almost as much as Marta does.

items.title: Bur Oak Farm, Woodstock, Illinois
items.text: Squash, chicories and eggs from a 40-acre farm, delivered every Tuesday and Friday.

items.title: Ellison Bay Orchard, Door County
items.text: Apples, Seckel pears and the first quince of the year for the olive oil cake.

items.title: Hollow Creek Dairy, Monroe, Wisconsin
items.text: Ricotta, butter and an alpine-style cheese aged for fourteen months.

items.title: Bayfield Fish Company, Lake Superior
items.text: Whitefish caught on Monday and on our pass by Wednesday afternoon.

items.title: Prairie Stone Mill, Champaign, Illinois
items.text: Heritage wheat and polenta, stone-milled for our pasta, bread and focaccia.

items.title: Kettle Ridge Farm, Kewaunee, Wisconsin
items.text: Two pasture-raised pigs a month, for the ragù, the sausage and the Sunday roast.

values.title: The Proofing Room seats up to 14
values.body:
Lindqvist’s Bakery left its dough to rise overnight in this room for 65 years. Today it holds one long oak table and a menu you plan with Marta.

  • Set menus from $75 per person, wine pairings from $45
  • Minimum spend of $900 Tuesday to Thursday, $1,400 Friday to Sunday
  • Lunch or dinner, on any day we are open

Write to events@hazelchicago.example with your date and group size, and we reply within a day.

image.alt: The Proofing Room set for twelve, with candles along a long oak table under exposed brick

values.quote: We booked the Proofing Room for my father’s eightieth. Fourteen of us, three generations, and the kitchen sent out an apple crostata with candles we never asked for.
values.name: Sofia Marchetti
values.role: Birthday dinner in the Proofing Room, March 2026

values.title: Questions about booking

items.question: Do you take walk-ins?
items.answer: Yes. The eight seats at the marble bar and two window tables are kept for walk-ins every night. Fridays and Saturdays are busiest after 7 pm.

items.question: Is there a deposit?
items.answer: Not for a regular table. For the tasting menu and groups of seven or more we hold the booking with a card and charge $25 per guest only if you cancel with less than 24 hours’ notice. The Proofing Room takes a 25% deposit, refunded in full up to seven days before.

items.question: Can you seat a large group?
items.answer: We seat up to ten in the dining room. For 8 to 14 guests with a room of your own, book the Proofing Room.

items.question: Can the kitchen cook around allergies and diets?
items.answer: Yes. Add them to your request and remind your server. We make gluten-free pasta every afternoon and can adapt most dishes for vegetarian, vegan, dairy-free and nut-free guests.

items.question: Are children welcome?
items.answer: Always. We have two high chairs and a half portion of any pasta for $10. Mention children when you book so we can save a chair.

items.question: How do we get there?
items.answer: We are on Clark Street between Foster and Farragut. The Berwyn Red Line station is a ten-minute walk, the 22 Clark bus stops outside, and there is metered parking along Clark.
